title: Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care) — Household and Income Measurement Settings
content:
## How household income is measured

The Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care) measures household income the same way on every tier (Riverbend Presumptive Charity Care; Riverbend Full Charity Care (0-200% FPL); Riverbend 80% Charity Discount (201-250% FPL); Riverbend 60% Charity Discount (251-300% FPL); Riverbend 40% Charity Discount (301-400% FPL); Riverbend Medical Hardship Assistance (above 400% FPL)):

| Setting | Value on every tier |
|---|---|
| Months of gross household income documented and annualized | 3 |
| Multiplier converting the documented months to annual income | 4 |
| Income figure used when both pay stubs and a tax return are supplied | the later-dated document |
| Who counts in the household | the IRS tax household |
| Poverty guideline used for household FPL percent | the HHS poverty guideline for the 48 contiguous states in effect on the application date |
| Documents accepted as proof of income | pay stubs for the last 90 days; federal tax return; Social Security award letter; unemployment benefit statement; zero-income attestation |

### Worked reading (hypothetical figures)

Three documented months of gross household income totalling 6,000.00 USD give an annual household income of 6,000.00 multiplied by 4, that is 24,000.00 USD. Where a household supplies both pay stubs and a federal tax return, the income figure comes from whichever of the two documents is dated later.

Any one of the five listed documents counts as proof of income.
